insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic attribution. This protocol settles at roughly $0.10 per verified receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that isn't a negotiating point, it's a structural difference in what you're actually buying.

insights.topic: Cookie deprecation creates an unmet need
insights.insight: With Chrome joining Safari and Firefox in killing cross-site cookies, the industry's primary targeting primitive is gone. Device fingerprinting is probabilistic and increasingly blocked; first-party data is accurate but silo-bound. Verified, identity-free purchase signals fill a gap that no current stack addresses.

insights.topic: Receipt as conversion event, not proxy
insights.insight: A cryptographically signed receipt eliminates the attribution problem entirely — no pixel, no lookback window, no modeled conversion. The receipt is the conversion event. That's a different category of evidence than anything the ad tech stack currently sells.

Amazon knows Amazon purchases. Walmart knows Walmart purchases. Neither knows the other. Any system that surfaces aggregate cross-ecosystem purchase behavior — without individual identity exposure — holds an information advantage that every brand and retailer currently lacks.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion pattern signals organic reach
insights.insight: Simultaneous activation in non-adjacent markets — Hawaii, Arizona, North Carolina, Arkansas entering the same cycle — follows social graph topology, not a paid acquisition funnel. For brand marketers, this means the signal base is expanding through word-of-mouth, not media spend.

Seven-day GMV sits at $30,191 across 657 receipts with a velocity ratio recovering to 0.868x after weeks of sub-0.75x compression. The trend line was rising throughout the compression period; the metric was lagging. The data now confirms the acceleration was real.
